b1-caudillismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Was a Caudillo?
b1-caudillismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the 19th century, and he asks what a caudillo was.
b1-caudillismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what a caudillo was.
cues: Say that a caudillo was a chief
Say what he had, with a relative clause
b1-caudillismo-01.target: Un caudillo era un jefe que tenía su propio ejército.
b1-caudillismo-01.english: A caudillo was a chief who had his own army.
b1-caudillismo-01.canDo: I can use relative clauses with *que* and *quien* to say who a caudillo was and who followed him.

b1-caudillismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Páez Held Power
b1-caudillismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading a book about Páez and asks how he kept his power.
b1-caudillismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Páez counted on.
b1-caudillismo-02.target: Páez contaba con la lealtad de los llaneros, y los jefes locales dependían de él.
b1-caudillismo-02.english: Páez counted on the loyalty of the llaneros, and the local chiefs depended on him.
b1-caudillismo-02.canDo: I can use verbs with a fixed preposition (*contar con*, *depender de*, *confiar en*) to describe a caudillo's network.

b1-caudillismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Montoneras
b1-caudillismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a class about the montoneras, and Carlos asks what happened when a war ended.
b1-caudillismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the men did when the war ended.
cues: Say when it happened, with cuando
b1-caudillismo-03.target: Cuando terminaba la guerra, los hombres volvían a su trabajo.
b1-caudillismo-03.english: When the war ended, the men went back to their work.
b1-caudillismo-03.canDo: I can use *cuando* and *mientras* to say what happened and what was going on at the same time.

b1-caudillismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Sarmiento Wrote
b1-caudillismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum, and she asks what Sarmiento wrote about the countryside.
cues: Say that he wrote it, with que
b1-caudillismo-04.target: Sarmiento escribió que el campo representaba la barbarie.
b1-caudillismo-04.english: Sarmiento wrote that the countryside represented barbarism.
b1-caudillismo-04.canDo: I can use reported speech (*dijo que*, *escribió que*) to say what people said and wrote about the caudillos.

b1-caudillismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Legacy of the Caudillos
b1-caudillismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you what many historians think about the caudillos after reading your class notes.
b1-caudillismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what turned out to be difficult.
cues: Say what turned out to be difficult
b1-caudillismo-05.target: Según muchos historiadores, resultó difícil crear instituciones fuertes.
b1-caudillismo-05.english: According to many historians, it turned out to be difficult to create strong institutions.
b1-caudillismo-05.canDo: I can use *resultar* + adjective to say what turned out to be difficult, useful or dangerous.

b1-caudillismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Caudillos
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing for a class, and she asks you about Rosas.
cues: Say that he was a landowner, with a relative clause
Say what he governed and until when
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.target: Rosas, que era hacendado, gobernó Buenos Aires hasta 1852.
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.english: Rosas, who was a landowner, governed Buenos Aires until 1852.
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the caudillos with relative clauses, verbs with a fixed preposition, *cuando* and *mientras*, reported speech and *resultar* + adjective.
